"With IKB, we welcome into the Group a franchise of exceptional quality, built on a century of proximity to clients, deep sector expertise and an unwavering commitment to the Mittelstand." text: Bumble in Talks to Be Taken Private in $1 Billion Deal, WSJ Says. (Bloomberg) -- Shares of dating-app company Bumble Inc. soared after the Wall Street Journal reported that it's in advanced talks to be taken private in a deal that values it at around $1 billion. The buyer is recently formed Ithaca Holdings and a deal could be announced as soon as this week, the Journal reported, citing unnamed people familiar with the matter. A takeover of Bumble would be one of its first major transactions, it said. A Bumble spokesperson did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Bumble was founded in 2014 by Whitney Wolfe Herd, a former Tinder cofounder, on the premise that only women could make the first move on the app. But Bumble, like many of its dating-app peers, has suffered user declines as young people have grown fatigued with online dating and have shown an interest in other forms of meeting, including in-person events. In August, Bumble ditched the women-go-first model, its latest move to boost user engagement. Shares of Bumble surged as much as 57% to $3.98 on Monday following the Wall Street Journal report, its biggest intraday jump since March 12

text: West Virginia. The West Virginia Office of the Insurance Commissioner published a bulletin informing insurers that the use of price optimization is unfairly discriminatory and in violation of state law. The OIC has heard of instances of insurers using price optimization to rate insurance policies in the state. Price optimization is the practice of using data of past consumer behavior in order to charge higher premiums. It analyzes how consumers have reacted to previous premium increases to predict how much the insurer can raise the premium before the consumer would shop for similar insurance from a different insurance company. Price optimization methods charge premiums based on data that is unrelated to a policyholder's risk of loss, which can result in two policyholders with the same loss history and risk profile being charged different premiums. The OIC has determined that the practice is unfairly discriminatory and in violation of West Virginia law. Insurers engaging in price optimization will face enforcement action.
